ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two composite figures made from the same five parts, respectively on the left side and the right side. Each figure contains one rectangle, two larger quarter-circles, and two smaller quarter-circles. Observing the outer boundary shows that, in the two figures, the arcs of all four quarter-circles are located on the outer outline; the exposure situations of the straight-line boundaries are different. On the outer boundary of the left figure there are two straight radius sides of large quarter-circles, as well as two straight radius sides of small quarter-circles. In the right figure, apart from the curves, the exposed straight-line part is only the bottom rectangle side. Reasoning: Because the two figures use the same two large quarter-circles and two small quarter-circles, and these arcs are all on the outer boundary, the total arc lengths of the two figures are the same, and when finding the perimeter difference the arc lengths cancel each other out. The rectangle is 5 cm × 10 cm, so the radius of a large quarter-circle is 10 cm, and the radius of a small quarter-circle is 5 cm. The exposed straight-line length of the left figure is 2×10+2×5=30 cm. The exposed straight-line length of the right figure is only the rectangle bottom side 10 cm. The perimeter difference of the two figures is 30−10=20 cm.

From the text, the rectangle is 5 cm by 10 cm, so the large quarter-circle radii match 10 cm and the small quarter-circle radii match 5 cm. Now count only exterior straight pieces from the image. In the left shape, the exposed straight parts are two large-quarter straight radii of length 10 cm and two small-quarter straight radii of length 5 cm, totaling 30 cm. In the right shape, the only exposed straight part is the bottom of the 5 by 10 rectangle, length 10 cm; the other straight sides are internal seams. Therefore the perimeter difference is 30 - 10 = 20 cm.

From the text, both figures are built from the same five pieces, so the sum of the perimeters of the separate pieces is identical for the two constructions. The only reason the final perimeters differ is that some straight edges are glued together internally; every shared internal seam removes that length twice from the outside perimeter. In the right-hand shape, the internal seams are the full horizontal join between the upper large quarters and the lower row, length 20 cm, the vertical join between the two large quarters, length 10 cm, and the two vertical joins between the small quarters and the rectangle, 5 + 5 cm; total internal seam length 40 cm.
